prerequisites: A fresh DOC-029 access account for this role, so seeded accounts keep their saved views.

Reviewer fixtures created by Daniel: a visible Contract whose PDF alone holds a unique word, a second visible Contract with that word in its title, and a Confidential Contract with that word in its title outside the fresh account's reach. The PDF text was searchable before the walkthrough started.
scenarios.expected: Results respect reach and the saved view restores its configuration; URL, chips, and rows agree. The hidden record never appears; no-match search and failed reads preserve understandable state.
scenarios.actual: 9 recorded steps passed on 3fa407e3 for a fresh Administrator. / focused Search. The header list and See all results showed the second Contract (title match) and the Document result v1 of the PDF Owned by its C- Contract, although that Contract's title lacks the word. The Document kind left only Document rows. Opening the result went to the Contract's Documents with the find text filled and the reader showing the file. The Confidential Contract never appeared in the header list, the results page or the API answer, and its direct link said Contract not found. Show more added 25 rows. A blocked next page said The next results could not be read. Try again. and kept the 25 rows, and Show more then worked. A blocked search showed Search could not load in the header and Search could not load. Try again. on the results page; a retry after recovery worked; an unmatched word said No matches. On Contracts, Filter > Owner > Daniel Okafor > Apply showed the Owner: Daniel Okafor chip, the Matches any selected value hint and only Daniel-owned rows. A Status filter narrowed the list further. The Title heading cycled ascending and descending. Back and Forward restored the sort marker and the chips with the URL. Remove Status filter and Clear all cleared filters, and Owner Me showed No contracts match these filters. Save as… with a Name stored the Owner filter, Title sort and a Columns move (Move Counterparty later). A change marked Modified; Discard unsaved changes restored the view; Save replaced it; Default view showed the built-in layout; selecting the view restored filter, sort and column order. Set as default reopened Contracts with the view. Rename… changed its name. A duplicate name was refused with You already have a view with that name on this list. A second browser for the same account opened the view. Delete… said the records are not touched and removed the view, and the Contract count stayed the same.

prerequisites: A fresh DOC-029 access account for this role, so seeded accounts keep their saved views.

Reviewer fixtures created by Daniel: a visible Contract whose PDF alone holds a unique word, a second visible Contract with that word in its title, and a Confidential Contract with that word in its title outside the fresh account's reach. The PDF text was searchable before the walkthrough started.
scenarios.expected: Results respect reach and the saved view restores its configuration; URL, chips, and rows agree. The hidden record never appears; no-match search and failed reads preserve understandable state.
scenarios.actual: 8 recorded steps passed on 3fa407e3 for a fresh Legal Team Member, with the same observations as the Administrator: title and PDF-only matches, the Document result naming its owning Contract and Version, find text filled in the reader, the Confidential Contract absent from search and refused by direct link, Show more and failed-read recovery, No matches, Owner and Status filters with chips, the Title sort cycle, Back and Forward, remove and Clear all, the empty filter message, and Save as…, Modified, Discard unsaved changes, Save, Default view, Set as default, Rename…, the duplicate-name refusal, another browser and Delete….

limitations: Independent agent walkthrough by a different agent from the author and the technical reviewer. It is not a human user study and not feature-owner approval.

The work lab is shared with other DOC-029 agents. Seeded records and counts changed during the run. The walkthrough created only accounts and records named DOC-029 access and changed no organisation settings. Nothing was deleted. Two earlier full runs are kept as walkthrough-r1-attempt1.json and walkthrough-r1-attempt2.json; their dispositions (a reviewer script timing error and shared-lab data drift) are in walkthrough-r1.json.
The lab app container runs with AUTH_RATE_LIMIT=off (lab configuration).
Column widths in a saved view, date filters (Includes both dates) and the transient Updating… state were not checked.

In the Columns menu, Move Title earlier and Move Title later do not respond to a mouse click, because the Title item is disabled and its buttons inherit pointer-events none. The walkthrough moved Counterparty instead. The article does not name Title, so this is not an article failure; it is reported separately as a possible product issue.
Search failures were produced by blocking requests in the browser, not by a server fault.

compatibilityReview.summary: I inspected the app diff from 3fa407e3 to 57e77e38, with messages/en-US.json; only the archived-owner text color in list columns and the Settings list panes changed, not search, filters, sort or saved views. I replayed the round 1 V-C04 walkthrough on the work2 lab for Administrator and Legal Team Member, and all 17 steps passed after one rerun for lab data volume.
